title: John Boorman's Point Blank - adultery in montage? (comment below)

commenti.body:
Does this film seem a little strange to you ? It does to me. A suppose the two scenes which give it away, the flashback of Lynn/Walker/Mel in a car. And the scene where "sister-in-law" Chris loses her nut with Walker, just before you see a clip on the TV - "it was your idea"...it was your idea?..basically the idea of an open marriage. I have overstated it as "adultery", technically this is not it.  
But in religious/legalistic terms that's what the director seems to convey, intentionally or not. Just to give you the summary of my interpretation in advance. A metaphorical film that suggest that when a third party enters a marriage your wife can no longer objectively-speaking be regarded as "wife", and in fact she now assumes the name, status and even face of sister.  
When that happens the person who was once spouse is commissioned to go about the business of putting end to the business of transgressing the law (in terms of the notion of sin) Obviously a spiritual/religious take on proceedings. But a valid interpretaton as any other.
